skill.name: shelter-lookup
skill.description: Search Japan's official GSI shelter datasets and rank designated emergency evacuation sites by hazard and distance from supplied coordinates.
skill.summary: Find nearby hazard-designated evacuation sites in Japan with approximate distances and municipal data update dates.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: Forty-seven alerts are false positives involving public GSI downloads, standard cache operations, Markdown formatting, and readable Japanese text. The shared temporary cache example permits local data poisoning because existing CSV files are trusted without ownership checks. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The documented shared temporary cache can accept attacker-planted evacuation data.
remediation.suggestion: Use the default private cache instead of a predictable shared directory. Enforce owner-only permissions and reject symlinked or foreign-owned cache directories and files.

content.user_title: Find Hazard-Designated Evacuation Sites in Japan
content.value_statement: Finding nearby evacuation sites requires matching the disaster type with current municipal records. This skill searches official GSI data and ranks matching sites from supplied coordinates.
actual_capabilities: Download official nationwide emergency-site and municipal update-history CSVs without an API key or login.
Filter emergency sites by eight disaster types, using English hazard keys or supported Japanese names.
Rank matching sites by Haversine distance from validated latitude and longitude, returning three by default or up to twenty.
Display site names, addresses, coordinates, hazard designations, and available municipal data update dates.
Reuse cached datasets, refresh them on request, and warn when cached files are more than seven days old.
Provide official designated-shelter download links and CSV parsing guidance for separate manual searches.
limitations: Coverage is limited to Japan's published GSI datasets; designation does not establish current opening status or capacity.
Distances are approximate straight-line measurements, not walking routes, travel times, or safe evacuation paths.
The skill does not calculate hazard-map coverage or flood depth, or decide whether evacuation is necessary.
Initial downloads and refreshes require internet access; cached records can become outdated, and municipal update dates may be unavailable.

use_cases.title: Prepare Nearby Evacuation Options
use_cases.description: Compare nearby sites designated for a chosen hazard and check municipal data update dates before making a household preparedness plan.

use_cases.title: Check Site Lists Near a Workplace
use_cases.description: Review hazard-designated emergency sites near workplace coordinates and distinguish approximate distance from actual evacuation-route suitability.

use_cases.title: Research Official Shelter Records
use_cases.description: Use official dataset links and structured CSV parsing guidance to compare emergency-site designations with designated-shelter records.

prompt_templates.title: Find Three Nearby Sites
prompt_templates.prompt: Find three flood-designated emergency sites near latitude [latitude] and longitude [longitude]. Include addresses, approximate straight-line distances, and municipal data update dates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Disaster Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Search separately for earthquake and tsunami sites near [latitude], [longitude]. Compare five results per hazard and retain each site's designation and update date.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh a Private Cache
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh the official datasets using the default private cache. Find ten landslide-designated sites near [latitude], [longitude] and report missing municipal update dates.

prompt_templates.title: Review Shelter and Emergency-Site Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Using official GSI CSVs, compare designated shelters and flood emergency sites in [municipality]. Use structured CSV parsing and report designations and available update dates.

output_examples.input: Illustrative test fixture: find the nearest flood-designated site from 35.00, 139.00 among near, far, and wrong hazard.
output: Nearest matching site: near, approximately 1.11 km from the supplied coordinates.
The wrong hazard fixture is excluded because it is not designated for floods.
Distance is straight-line distance, not walking distance. These are synthetic test records, not real evacuation recommendations.

output_examples.input: Illustrative cache-age check: inspect files that are one day old and ten days old.
output: The ten-day-old cache is flagged; the one-day-old cache is not.
Cached records may miss municipal updates. Refresh the official datasets before relying on current designations.

best_practices: Use the default private cache and avoid predictable shared temporary directories that other users can populate.
Specify the correct hazard and include municipal data update dates; refresh old caches before reviewing current designations.
Confirm opening status and evacuation routes with official municipal guidance; treat calculated distance only as an approximate comparison.
anti_patterns: Treating the closest site as safe for every disaster type.
Presenting straight-line distance as walking distance, travel time, or a verified safe route.
Using stale cached records as proof of current opening status or as the sole basis for an evacuation decision.

faq.question: Which area does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It searches nationwide Japanese datasets published by GSI for municipal designated shelters and emergency evacuation sites.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or additional packages?
faq.answer: No API key or login is required. The bundled lookup script uses Python 3 and standard-library modules only.

faq.question: Which hazards can the lookup script filter?
faq.answer: It supports floods, landslides, storm surges, earthquakes, tsunamis, large fires, inland flooding, and volcanic phenomena.

faq.question: Does the distance indicate a safe walking route?
faq.answer: No. It is an approximate Haversine distance. The script does not account for roads, rivers, cliffs, closures, or route safety.

faq.question: How are data updates handled?
faq.answer: The script displays available municipal update dates and warns about caches older than seven days. Refreshing requires an explicit request.

faq.question: Can the skill tell me whether to evacuate now?
faq.answer: No. Follow official warnings and municipal evacuation announcements. Dataset designation alone does not confirm that a facility is currently open.
